stories.title: Add the needle's metal absorption maths shared by both renderers
stories.description: In src/render/pipeline.ts add step 2b of the ORDER OF STEPS: the needle. New numbers: NEEDLE_RADIUS_MM (draft 0.35, the same for every needle; see notes), NEEDLE_ABSORPTION_PER_MM (draft, strong enough that the needle is clearly darker than bone) and MAX_NEEDLE_SEGMENTS (64). Add resampleShaft(points): the shaft curve (hub → tip, NeedleState.shaft) as at most MAX_NEEDLE_SEGMENTS + 1 points evenly spaced along its length, keeping the hub and the tip exactly. Add needlePathLength(rayOrigin, rayDir, points): the length of the ray inside the tube of radius NEEDLE_RADIUS_MM around those segments (per segment: from the ray-to-segment distance, the chord through the tube, never more than the segment length plus a diameter). The needle absorbs wherever it is, also outside the volume's box. Plain TypeScript, no browser code.
acceptance: Unit test: resampleShaft of a 400-point curve gives at most 65 points with the same first and last point and equal spacing within 1%
Unit test: a ray crossing a straight segment at right angles through its axis gives a path length of 2 × NEEDLE_RADIUS_MM (±1%); a ray that passes 1 mm away gives 0
Unit test: a ray along the segment's own line gives the segment's length (±1%), not infinity
Unit test: an empty or one-point shaft gives 0
stories.notes: Owner decision 2026-11-13 (accepted every F5–F7 planning default): one tube width (0.35 mm radius) for every needle.

stories.title: Add the needle to the CPU reference X-ray image
stories.description: drrCpu.ts (renderDrrCpu and transmissionAt) takes an optional needle option (the shaft points). Its absorption is total += needlePathLength(…) × NEEDLE_ABSORPTION_PER_MM along each ray, from the source to the detector position, after resampleShaft. Without the option the image is unchanged.
acceptance: Unit test (phantom, pose 0°/0°): a straight needle lying across the beam in muscle makes the pixel at its projected middle darker than the pixels 5 px to either side, and darker than the same pixel with no needle
Unit test: with no needle option, every pixel equals the image before this story (the existing CPU tests stay green unchanged)
Unit test: a needle outside the volume's box (in the air above the back) still darkens its pixels

stories.title: Add the needle to the GPU X-ray shader
stories.description: drrGpu.ts take() accepts the needle shaft (resampled with resampleShaft, sent as a uniform array of at most 65 points plus a count) and adds the same needle absorption as the CPU reference, on every ray, including outside the volume's box. fluoroCanvas.ts passes store.needle?.shaft at each exposure. Add zone screen-test helpers in tests/e2e/render/ to put a hand-made NeedleState into the store (the dev-server store module trick; like tests/e2e/view3d/view3dPage.ts, but the render zone's own copy).
acceptance: Screen test (both set-ups, phantom, pose 0°/0°): with a hand-made straight needle across the beam in soft tissue, a new image's pixels along the projected needle are darker than the pixels 5 px to the side (F7.1)

Screen test (both set-ups): the GPU image with the needle matches the CPU reference (same needle and pose, no noise): in a 21×21 px box around the needle's projected middle the mean difference is at most 3% of the grey range (as in cpuMatch.spec.ts), and the needle is darker than its surroundings in both
Screen test (both set-ups): with no needle the image is unchanged (existing render screen tests stay green unchanged)

stories.title: Keep the needle frozen in the held image until the next exposure
stories.description: The needle drawn in the image is the needle at the moment of the exposure: fluoroCanvas.ts copies store.needle's shaft when an exposure happens; later needle changes do not redraw the held image, and display changes (invert, flip, rotate) re-show the held image with the old needle. Add the copied needle tip to the 'render' debug getter's lastImage (needleTip, or null).
acceptance: Screen test (both set-ups): take an image with a needle; move the needle in the store; the canvas pixel fingerprint is unchanged and lastImage.needleTip is the old tip
Screen test (both set-ups): after the next image the fingerprint changes and needleTip is the new tip
Screen test (both set-ups): turning Invert on after moving the needle shows the inverted image with the OLD needle position (its pixels are lighter than their surroundings at the old place)

stories.title: Check that the needle tip lands where the geometry says
stories.description: Screen test: for 5 poses drawn with createRandom(seed) (oblique −40…40°, tilt −20…20°), a hand-made needle with its tip in soft tissue of the phantom is imaged; the tip pixel found in the image (the needle pixel — darker than the same image with no needle by a fixed margin — farthest from the hub's projection) is within 2 px of geometry.project(tip). Default display settings. Put the tip-finding code in the zone's test helpers.
acceptance: Screen test (both set-ups): all 5 seeded poses pass within 2 px
Screen test (both set-ups): the same seed always gives the same 5 poses

stories.title: Check down-the-beam and angled needles look right
stories.description: Screen test at a fixed depth (needle 40 mm inside the phantom, entry on the back): a straight needle exactly along the ray from the source through its entry point projects to a spot whose longest extent (needle pixels as in F7-S5) is at most 4 px; the same needle at 30° to that ray appears as a line longer than 20 px. This is the feature's last 'test only' story before the canvas tap.
acceptance: Screen test (both set-ups): down the beam, the needle's pixel spot is no longer than 4 px
Screen test (both set-ups): at 30° to the beam, the needle's line is longer than 20 px

stories.title: Report taps and clicks on the fluoro image as image pixels
stories.description: For the needle zone's Mark entry tool (F5.2): a click (desktop) or tap (tablet) on the fluoro canvas while an image is held emits the 'imageTap' bus event with the pixel of the image AS TAKEN: the canvas position scaled to 512×512, then the display flips/rotation undone (unorientPixel in orientation.ts), then magnification undone (the detector position, pipeline step 1), so createProjection(store.lastImagePose).unproject(pixel) gives the ray that made that pixel. Nothing is emitted before the first image or on a collimated (covered) pixel. Put the mapping in a plain function with a unit test. This is the feature's last loop story: run the whole check.
acceptance: Unit test: with default settings the canvas pixel (300, 200) maps to (300, 200); with flip left-right it maps to (211, 200); with magnification 2 the canvas pixel (356, 256) maps to (306, 256); with rotation 90° the mapping is the inverse of orientPixel
Screen test (both set-ups; click on desktop, tap on tablet): after one image, tapping the canvas centre emits one imageTap of (256, 256) ±1 px (listened for through the dev-server store module)
Screen test (both set-ups): before the first image a tap emits nothing
npm run check passes
stories.verify: npx vitest run tests/render/imageTap.test.ts && npx playwright test tests/e2e/render/imageTap.spec.ts && npm run check
stories.notes: Owner decision 2026-11-13 (accepted every F5–F7 planning default): the bus event `imageTap` (payload ImageTap { x, y } from src/core/store.ts) is on the shared contract. Unblocked.
